items.title: Network pharmacology and bioinformatics analysis of the potential mechanism of morin against myocardial infarction.
items.abstract: As a typical natural flavonoid compound, morin exerts definite cardioprotective effects. Nevertheless, its specific molecular regulatory mechanisms in the treatment of myocardial infarction have not been fully elucidated. This study combined network pharmacology and bioinformatic strategies to screen candidate targets of morin as well as genes closely associated with myocardial infarction across diverse databases. Further validations were implemented via functional enrichment analysis, three machine learning models including LASSO regression, SVM-RFE and random forest algorithm, immune infiltration assessment and molecular docking verification. Through a multi-step screening process, six candidate genes were identified, including ARG1, CDK6, CXCR1, CYP1B1, MMP9, and PFKFB3. These candidate genes are enriched in inflammation- and metabolism-related signaling pathways, including the TNF, AMPK, HIF-1, and IL-17 pathways, as well as pathways involved in arachidonic acid metabolism and phagocytosis. Immune association analysis suggests that these genes are associated with neutrophils, macrophages, and mast cells. Molecular docking simulations predict a potential binding interaction between mulberry pigment and these target proteins. Morin may alleviate damage caused by myocardial infarction by regulating immune and inflammatory responses, metabolic processes, and tissue remodeling.

items.title: Prevalence of excess adiposity and clinical obesity in a Mexican nationally representative survey.
items.abstract: Body mass index (BMI) alone may underestimate clinically relevant obesity because it does not capture central fat distribution. We compared obesity prevalence in Mexico using BMI-only criteria, adiposity-confirmed criteria, and the clinical obesity definition proposed by the Lancet Diabetes and Endocrinology Commission. We conducted a population-based, cross-sectional study of 13,160 adults aged 18 years or older who participated in the 2018-2019 Mexican National Health and Nutrition Survey (ENSANUT). We estimated obesity prevalence using survey-weighted analyses that accounted for the complex sampling design. The weighted prevalence of obesity based on BMI was 34.5% (95% CI, 33.1-35.9), while 32.6% (95% CI, 31.3-34.0) met criteria for clinical obesity. One quarter of individuals with clinical obesity had a BMI under 30 kg/m2, a phenotype more common among older adults and substantially more common among women than men. Half of adults with a BMI under 30 kg/m2 showed elevated central adiposity. BMI alone underestimates clinically relevant obesity in Mexican adults. Adding waist-based measurements could improve the identification of individuals with excess fat and metabolic risk, both in clinical settings and population monitoring.

items.title: Endurance Exercise Training Before Myocardial Infarction Reduces Decline of Myocardial Function in Old Mice.
items.abstract: Pre-infarction endurance training reduces scar formation and adverse cardiac remodeling in rodents; however, evidence is largely restricted to young animals. Whether these benefits extend to aged individuals, the population most affected by myocardial infarction (MI), remains unclear. We investigated the effects of 6 weeks of endurance exercise training prior to MI in aged mice (20 months). C57BL/6 mice were randomized to exercise (EX-MI, n=11; treadmill running 30 min/day, 5 days/week) or sedentary conditions (SED-MI, n=12). MI was induced by permanent ligation of the left anterior descending artery. FDG PET imaging was performed on days 5 and 7 post MI, and cardiac structure and function were evaluated by MRI at day 28. Histological analyses were performed ex vivo. Exercise training resulted in smaller and thicker infarct scars compared with sedentary controls. Despite similar lef t ventricular dilation, EX-MI mice showed significantly improved systolic function, with higher ejection fraction and stroke volume. This was supported by enhanced global longitudinal and radial strain rates. Likewise, regional deformation analysis demonstrated higher circumferential and radial strain within the scar. FDG uptake was increased in the infarct region at day 7. Additionally, remote myocardium was thicker and exhibited greater radial deformation in exercised animals. Our study shows that short time endurance exercise training in older mice prior to acute MI reduces post-MI left ventricular remodeling, scar size, and scar thinning. Myocardial contractility in both the remote and infarct areas were preserved by endurance training, potentially reflecting an enhanced compensatory capacity induced by pre-infarction exercise training.

items.title: Interpreting Biomarker Dynamics After Acute Heart Failure: Lessons From PREMIER.
Long-term antibody responses to Vibrio cholerae across natural infection, vaccination, and challenge: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Cholera is a critical global health threat, with significant impact on low- and middle-income countries. Clinical surveillance is limited by nonspecific symptoms, dependence on care-seeking, and availability of microbiological diagnostics, making burden estimation difficult. Serosurveillance is a potential solution, but the design and interpretation of cross-sectional seroepidemiological studies are currently limited by a lack of knowledge of longitudinal antibody trajectories. We systematically reviewed literature from 1980 to 2025 containing longitudinal antibody measurements in humans following exposure to Vibrio cholerae O1/O139 and associated vaccines. To account for variability in assay scales and units across studies, antibody responses were compared using fold changes in titers relative to baseline values. Fifty-eight studies representing adults and children from 2 low-income (2 studies), 5 lower-middle-income (29 studies), 3 upper-middle-income (5 studies), and 6 high-income (23 studies) countries were included. Nineteen studies followed natural infection, 42 involved vaccination, and 6 were human challenge models, with some overlap. Antibody responses following infection were higher than those induced by vaccination, particularly against O-specific polysaccharide (OSP). Younger children exhibited higher peak fold-change IgA responses to Cholera-toxin B-subunit (CTB) than older children and adults across infection and vaccine studies. Following vaccination, individuals from high-income countries showed higher IgA, IgG, and vibriocidal fold-change responses compared to those from lower-income settings. Limited data from challenge studies revealed slower decay of IgG compared to IgA and IgM. This review enhances our understanding of longitudinal immune responses to V. cholerae, highlighting variability in antibody kinetics across age groups, geographic regions, and study designs, and informs the design and interpretation of seroepidemiological studies of cholera.

items.title: Molecular subtyping, prognostic model construction, and immune microenvironment analysis of cervical squamous cell carcinoma based on metabolic health and disease prevention.
items.abstract: Background: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) development is modulated not only by HPV infection but also by host metabolic health. Purpose and method: This study characterised disulfidptosis-related genes (DRGs) in 241 TCGA-CESC and 300 GSE44001 patients to build a prognostic model and interpret it within a metabolic health-oriented prevention framework. Seventeen differentially expressed DRGs, enriched in glycolysis, fatty acid metabolism, and redox homeostasis, defined three metabolic-distinct molecular subtypes. Result: A six-gene DRG-score (DSTN, TLN1, MTHFD1L, MYH10, TXN, SLC7A11) and nomogram predicted prognosis effectively (C-index 0.747/0.665; 1-year AUC 0.835). High-risk tumours showed an immunosuppressed phenotype (immunotherapy response 20.0% vs. 71.9%) concordant with obesity- and diabetes-associated immune dysfunction, and reduced sensitivity to methotrexate, implicating one-carbon metabolism. Conclusion: These findings indicate that metabolic health optimisation-weight control, nutrition, physical activity, and management of diabetes and dyslipidemia-constitutes a modifiable pillar of CSCC prevention complementary to HPV vaccination and screening, warranting prospective validation with DRG-based stratification.

items.title: Human papillomavirus vaccination coverage among adolescent girls and young women living with HIV in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Human Papilloma Virus (HPV)-attributable cancers disproportionately affect adolescent girls and young women living with HIV (AGYWLHIV) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet HPV vaccination coverage in this subpopulation remains suboptimal. This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the pooled prevalence of HPV vaccination coverage among AGYWLHIV in LMICs. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), and Web of Science for observational studies published between January 2014 and December 2025. A random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate the pooled prevalence of HPV vaccination coverage. Subgroup analyses by age group and vaccine type were conducted, while HPV vaccination delivery platforms were summarised descriptively. Publication bias and sensitivity analyses were also performed, and statistical heterogeneity was evaluated using the I² statistic. A total of 8 studies involving 1,059 AGYWLHIV were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled HPV vaccination coverage among AGYWLHIV in LMICs was 28.6% (95% CI: 20.3%-38.7%) based on a random-effects model, with substantial heterogeneity across studies (I² = 87.0%, p < 0.0001). Exploratory subgroup analysis by age yielded HPV vaccination coverage of 90.3% (95% CI: 74.2%-98.0%) among participants aged 9-14 years (1 study; n = 31) and 19.2% (95% CI: 11.0%-31.4%) among those aged 15-26 years (4 studies; n = 250). Exploratory descriptive findings indicated that HPV vaccination was delivered through health facilities, schools, community outreach, and combinations of these approaches. However, differences in denominators limited direct comparisons between delivery platforms. The available evidence from studies conducted in LMICs indicates low HPV vaccination coverage among AGYWLHIV. Integrating HPV vaccination into routine HIV care may represent a potentially useful strategy to improve access and reduce missed vaccination opportunities among AGYWLHIV and should be further evaluated alongside broader efforts supported by strong political commitment and multisectoral collaboration. PROSPERO Number: CRD420251068971.

items.title: From Allergy to Tumor Immunology: The Dual Role of Antigen-Specific IgE - Mechanisms, Challenges, and Prospects for Clinical Translation.
items.abstract: Allergic reactions and tumor immunity have conventionally been regarded as opposing poles of immune responsiveness, and antigen-specific IgE (AS-IgE) has been defined almost exclusively by its pathogenic role in type I hypersensitivity. Accumulating evidence now indicates that AS-IgE is not a single-function mediator of allergy but also participates in antitumor immune surveillance, raising the question of whether this allergic effector molecule can be redirected as a tool for cancer immunotherapy. This review systematically explores the dual role of AS-IgE in allergic reactions and tumor immunity, focusing on the feasibility, underlying mechanisms and current obstacles of its clinical translation. Beyond mediating mast cell degranulation, AS-IgE can engage FcεRI on monocytes and macrophages to elicit ADCC and ADCP, thereby reshaping the TME and potentiating CD8+ T cell-mediated antitumor activity. Conversely, the same FcεRI-dependent axis may skew immunity toward Th2-polarized responses that foster local immunosuppression and contribute to tumor promotion, while the persistent risk of inducing allergic reactions remains the principal barrier to therapeutic application. Engineering strategies designed to optimize the molecule, particularly IgE desialylation, which reduces sensitivity to allergenic stimulation while preserving effector function, are summarized as routes toward safer use. Unresolved questions concerning how to balance anticancer efficacy against allergic and protumorigenic risk are critically evaluated, and future research directions are proposed, emphasizing the prioritization of safety optimization and the rational combination of AS-IgE with immune checkpoint inhibitors. Clinical translation of AS-IgE requires that reduction of allergenic risk be established as the primary prerequisite, with combination regimens incorporating immune checkpoint inhibitors explored to amplify and sustain antitumor efficacy; future research should be more closely aligned with patient individual differences and the characteristics of the tumor microenvironment across diverse populations, so that the dual role of AS-IgE can be precisely regulated and this molecule can ultimately move from the laboratory to the clinic.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Sublingual Versus Subcutaneous Immunotherapy for Patients With Allergic Rhinitis with Asthma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) and asthma are common chronic respiratory disorders that frequently coexist. Allergen immunotherapy is a disease-modifying treatment; however, the comparative efficacy and safety of subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT) and sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) remain uncertain in patients with concomitant AR and asthma. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies directly comparing SCIT and SLIT in patients with AR and concomitant asthma were eligible. Outcomes included symptom scores, medication use, reported asthma exacerbations or worsening events, visual analog scale (VAS) scores, immunological markers, and adverse events. Nine studies were included in the systematic review, 7 of which contributed to the meta-analysis. Sublingual immunotherapy was associated with fewer reported asthma exacerbations or worsening events than SCIT (odds ratio [OR], 0.28; 95% CI, 0.09-0.89; moderate certainty evidence). Subcutaneous immunotherapy was associated with greater improvement in VAS scores (mean difference [MD], 1.80; 95% CI, 0.82-2.78; low certainty evidence). No statistically significant differences were observed in the total rhinitis symptom score (MD, 0.44; 95% CI, -0.14-1.02; very low certainty evidence), total medication score (MD, -0.48; 95% CI, -1.12 to 0.16; low certainty evidence), or total asthma symptom score (MD, -0.24; 95% CI, -1.03 to 0.55; very low certainty evidence). No statistically significant differences were found in systemic reactions (OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.05-1.43), skin reactions (OR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.41-1.28), nausea or vomiting (OR, 1.25; 95% CI, 0.23-6.94), or withdrawal rates (OR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.21-2.51). Limited comparative evidence suggests that SLIT may be associated with fewer reported asthma-worsening events than SCIT, whereas SCIT may be associated with greater improvement in VAS scores. However, these findings were based on a small number of clinically heterogeneous studies using nonstandardized outcome definitions. No clear differences were observed in rhinitis symptoms, medication use, asthma symptom scores, or most safety outcomes. Further high-quality head-to-head randomized controlled trials are needed.

items.title: Chronic Hepatitis B and Delta Coinfection in a Person With Opioid Use Disorder: Missed Prevention Opportunities and Implications for Addiction Practice.
items.abstract: People who inject drugs are disproportionately affected by hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infections. Missed HBV vaccination opportunities and delayed HDV testing in patients with substance use disorder can result in preventable liver disease. A 46-year-old White man with opioid use disorder (OUD), housing instability, chronic HBV, resolved hepatitis C virus infection, and injection drug use presented with newly decompensated liver disease. Review of prior records revealed documented HBV nonimmunity 9 years earlier during multiple outpatient encounters for OUD care and hepatitis C virus evaluation, yet no HBV vaccination was administered across 6 clinical visits. Following a lapse in care, he was diagnosed with chronic HBV 6 years later. An equivocal HDV antibody was identified the following year, but confirmatory HDV RNA testing was delayed by 2 more years, ultimately revealing high-level HDV viremia. He was initiated on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine with significant HBV viral load reduction but required hepatology referral for decompensated liver disease and transplant consideration. This case illustrates repeated missed opportunities for guideline-recommended HBV vaccination and timely HBV/HDV screening in a person with OUD, contributing to preventable decompensated liver disease. Addiction medicine settings are well positioned to deliver these recommended preventive services and to link patients to specialty care.

items.title: Initial uptake of doxycycline for the prevention of bacterial sexually transmitted infections (doxy PEP) in publicly funded New York City (NYC) Sexual Health Clinics.
items.abstract: With inequitable uptake of other biomedical interventions, understanding doxy PEP uptake and related patient-level factors is critical for optimal service provision. Among men-who-have-sex-with-men and transgender women with no prior doxy PEP use who attended NYC Sexual Health Clinics (SHCs) [April 2024-May 2025], we 1) describe the doxy PEP cascade (i.e., clinical evaluation for, offer of, acceptance of, and provision of doxy PEP) by patient indications (past-year history of bacterial STI, multiple sex partners in past 3 months, HIV status, engagement in sex work, interest in doxy PEP), demographics, and current HIV PrEP use, and 2) factors associated with uptake. Of 3,560 patients who presented with doxy PEP indications, 69.7% (2,481/3,560) received doxy PEP. Retention rates were >95% at each cascade step, with two exceptions. Of patients with clinical evaluations for doxy PEP, 86.6% (2,863/3,304) had their candidacy confirmed. While 98.8% of these patients (2,829/2,863) were offered doxy PEP, 89.2% (2,523/2,829) accepted. Doxy PEP receipt was associated with having two indications (adjusted prevalence ratio (aPR): 1.74, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.61-1.89) or ≥3 indications (aPR 2.07, 95% CI: 1.92-2.25) versus one, and with HIV PrEP use (aPR 0.90, 95% CI: 0.86-0.95, no PrEP versus PrEP). NYC SHCs serve a large population of doxy PEP candidates, with nearly 2,500 initiates over approximately one year. Uptake did not vary by patient demographics (e.g., age, race/ethnicity), but other disparities were noted. Such findings can inform refinements to clinic systems that can lead to higher-impact outcomes of doxy PEP implementation.

items.title: Barriers and facilitators along the continuum of care among people living with hepatitis B in EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK: A scoping review.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) represents a significant global health burden, with approximately 14 million infected individuals in EU/EEA countries. The alarmingly low proportions diagnosed, linked to, engaged and retained in care underscore the necessity for further evidence on HBV care continuum dynamics, as emphasized in the new World Health Organisation guidelines for HBV. We conducted a scoping review to identify and describe research addressing modifiable barriers and facilitators related to the care continuum for people living with HBV infection in EU/EEA countries, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. We pre-specified our methods in a protocol, conducted the review in line with a methodological guide, searched six databases, selected eligible studies in duplicate, and summarized data descriptively. We included 24 studies, of which most were published after 2016 and were observational quantitative studies. The studies included about 25,000 participants from 11 countries, primarily immigrants living with HBV infection, of which 90% had chronic HBV infection. Six studies covered the perspectives of healthcare professionals. For each study, we determined which stage(s) of the continuum of care the study attended to, finding that nine provided outcome data on two or three stages of care. While 14 studies concerned linkage to care (stage 3) and ten studies retention in care (stage 5), few investigated testing (stage 1), referral (stage 2) or engagement in care (stage 4). We grouped the studies' results according to the five care continuum stages and found that a handful of barriers consistently emerged across multiple continuum stages: systemic healthcare constraints (including resource constraints, deprioritization of HBV), provider knowledge deficiencies, and patients' limited understanding of the condition and negative perceptions of HBV. More research is necessary and must encompass a broader spectrum of at-risk populations and income settings to better align with the epidemiological distribution of HBV burden across Europe.

items.title: Perceptions About Hepatitis C and Barriers and Enablers to Screening and Treatment among Punjabi Immigrants to Canada: A Theory-Informed Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Canada aims to eliminate hepatitis C virus (HCV) by 2030, yet screening and treatment uptake remains low. Immigrants from high-prevalence countries account for approximately 35% of cases and often have low screening rates, associated with delayed diagnosis, poorer outcomes, and increased healthcare costs. Given the large Punjabi immigrant population in Canada and limited research on their experiences with HCV care, this study explored beliefs and experiences related to HCV screening and treatment. A Project Advisory Group was engaged to inform all phases of the research. We used a qualitative- descriptive design informed by the Common-Sense Self-Regulation Model and the Theoretical Domains Framework. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with immigrants from Punjab and Haryana, India (with and without HCV) in Montreal. Data collection continued until thematic saturation was reached. Transcripts were independently coded by two researchers, and key themes were identified. Sixteen participants (eight men, eight women) were interviewed, including eight who had been screened for HCV (of which four tested positive and three received treatment). Participants described varying levels of familiarity with HCV and its management. The absence of symptoms delayed care-seeking. Stigma and concerns about disclosure also shaped conversations about HCV. Participants described practical challenges, including language barriers and difficulties accessing primary care. Family support and trust in healthcare providers facilitated engagement with screening and treatment. Improving HCV care among immigrants is essential for meeting Canada's elimination goals. Our findings highlight the need for approaches that address multiple factors influencing HCV care, including awareness, stigma, communication, and access to services.

items.title: HCC risk in HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B: impact of low baseline HBsAg and poor on-treatment decline.
items.abstract: The association between hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development during long-term nucleos(t)ide analog (NUC) treatment remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) levels and HCC incidence in patients with baseline HBeAg positivity who were receiving NUC treatment. Overall, 951 patients with chronic hepatitis B with baseline HBeAg positivity who had received NUC treatment for at least 1 year were included. The outcomes evaluated were HCC incidence and HBsAg loss (< 0.05 IU/mL) according to baseline and on-treatment HBsAg kinetics. Over a 14.7-year median treatment duration, 98 patients developed HCC. A low baseline qHBsAg level (< 10,000 IU/mL) was significantly associated with a three to four times higher risk of HCC than a high baseline qHBsAg level (≥ 10,000 IU/mL). Baseline HBV DNA levels also showed the association with HCC in univariate analysis as previously reported. qHBsAg was superior to HBV DNA for predicting the risk of HCC in multivariable analysis and receiver operating characteristic curves analysis. Furthermore, patients with low baseline qHBsAg levels and low decline in qHBsAg levels during the first year of treatment independently had a high risk of HCC. Conversely, the HBsAg seroclearance rates were lower in patients with low baseline qHBsAg levels and low decline in qHBsAg levels. Low baseline qHBsAg levels and poor decline in qHBsAg were associated with a high risk of HCC, and the rarity of HBsAg loss in patients with baseline HBeAg positivity who were receiving NUC treatment.

items.title: Ultrasound-Based Physiological Sensing: Challenges, Strategies, and Applications.
items.abstract: Ultrasound is well suited to repeated deep-tissue imaging, but it rarely measures local biochemical conditions directly. Stimuli-responsive chemistry enables materials to respond to physiological cues through physicochemical changes, yet these changes are not necessarily detectable by ultrasound. Multiscale structural organization can bridge this gap by translating and amplifying molecular or nanoscale responses into larger-scale material changes that produce detectable acoustic signals. The field is progressing from proof-of-concept demonstrations of material responses towards integrated sensing platforms. Advances across these platforms include bioresorption, multiparametric sensing, and repeated measurements over defined periods in animal models. This review examines how responsive chemistry and multiscale structural design jointly enable ultrasound-readable physiological sensing. It also considers the requirements for reliable operation in vivo. Looking ahead, integration with wearable and conformal ultrasound interfaces, soft robotic systems, and AI-assisted decoding could enable longitudinal, personalized, and multiparametric sensing across internal organs and tissue interfaces.

items.title: Cinnamaldehyde induces NRF2-dependent ferroptosis to sensitize hepatocellular carcinoma to sorafenib.
items.abstract: The efficacy of systemic therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is severely limited by strong antioxidant defense systems. This study aimed to investigate the mechanism by which cinnamaldehyde (CA) induces cytotoxicity in HCC cells and explore its potential to enhance the therapeutic index of sorafenib. Network pharmacology, molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were used to identify and validate drug-protein targets. Cell viability, migration, lipid ROS and mitochondrial ultrastructure were assessed alongside ferroptotic markers, including iron, glutathione (GSH), and lipid peroxidation. The NRF2 pathway and xCT transport function were analyzed via Western blotting, immunofluorescence, nuclear fractionation, luciferase reporter, and glutamate release assays. CA functioned as a specific inducer of ferroptosis- reversible by ferrostatin-1 and liproxstatin-1 -characterized by iron overload and GSH depletion. Mechanistically, high-dose CA triggered a lethal reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst driven by the impairment of NRF2 nuclear translocation, preventing downstream antioxidant activation. Consequently, cellular defense collapsed despite a futile compensatory upregulation of xCT (SLC7A11). CA also synergized with sorafenib in HCC cells. By effectively blocking NRF2 nuclear entry, CA dismantles genomic redox defenses, creating a vulnerability that significantly potentiates the efficacy of sorafenib. This reveals a novel mechanism wherein CA drives ferroptosis via "nuclear blockade", offering a dual-hit therapeutic strategy.

items.title: Robotic versus laparoscopic simultaneous resection for rectal cancer and synchronous liver metastases: the RAPTOR study.
items.abstract: Simultaneous resection of rectal cancer and synchronous liver metastases, despite being technically demanding, is increasingly performed in select patients. Robotic surgery may offer advantages over laparoscopy in complex procedures; however, evidence comparing robotic and laparoscopic simultaneous rectal and liver resection is limited. We compared perioperative, oncologic, and survival outcomes between robotic and laparoscopic approaches. The National Cancer Database (2015-2023) was queried to identify patients with stage IV rectal adenocarcinoma and isolated synchronous liver metastases who underwent simultaneous minimally invasive resection of the primary tumor and liver metastases. The primary outcome was conversion to open surgery. Secondary outcomes included length of stay, circumferential resection margin (CRM) status, surgical margin status, lymph node harvest, readmission, short-term mortality, and overall survival. The two groups were matched using 1:1 propensity-score matching. Among 940 patients, 535 underwent robotic and 405 laparoscopic resection. After matching, 312 patients remained in each group. Robotic surgery was associated with a lower conversion rate (4.2% vs. 14.1%, p  <  0.001) and shorter median hospital stay (4 vs. 5 days, p  =  0.005). CRM negativity, adequate lymph node harvest, negative surgical margins, 30-day readmission, and 30- and 90-day mortality did not differ significantly between groups. No statistically significant difference in overall survival was observed. In multivariable analysis of the unmatched cohort, robotic surgery remained independently associated with lower odds of conversion to open surgery (OR 0.407, 95% CI 0.242-0.683; p  =  0.001). Robotic simultaneous rectal and liver resection was associated with lower conversion rates and shorter hospitalization compared with laparoscopy, without statistically significant differences in measured oncologic outcomes or overall survival. Given the absence of detailed information regarding hepatic operative complexity and reasons for conversion, these findings should be interpreted as associations and warrant validation in studies with more granular operative data.

items.title: Organoid-Based Strategy for Exploration of Cancer-Related Early Signatures of Low-Dose Methylmercury Exposure.
items.abstract: Methylmercury (MeHg) compounds are classified as Group 2B agents, possibly carcinogenic to humans by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), and as Group C possible human carcinogens by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA), but the carcinogenic implications of environmentally relevant low-dose exposure remain unclear. Here, we established a population-informed organoid-based strategy to explore the potential of low-dose MeHg exposure leading to cancer incidence. A National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)-based analysis revealed nonlinear associations of blood MeHg with overall cancer history with increased predicted cancer probability around 5.39 μg/L for MeHg. Liver organoid experiments showed that low-dose MeHg did not cause overt short-term cytotoxicity but induced DNA damage and stress-response signatures after prolonged exposure. Transcriptomic analysis further linked low-dose MeHg exposure to cancer-related stress pathways, including reactive oxygen species (ROS) associated chemical carcinogenesis, p53 signaling, DNA repair, mitochondrial stress, and cell-cycle regulation. These results indicate that low-dose MeHg exposure could trigger early biological responses related to cancer-associated processes before apparent cytotoxicity occurs. This study supports organoid models as a human-relevant strategy for linking population exposure signals with tissue-level toxicological evidence in MeHg research and provides a potentially adaptable framework for evaluating subtle health effects of low-dose environmental pollutants.

items.title: Liver Transplant Waitlist Outcomes Among HCC Exception Candidates with Durable Radiologic Complete Response to Locoregional Therapy.
items.abstract: Some hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients achieve radiologic complete response (CR) after locoregional therapy (LRT) yet retain exception priority despite potentially lower dropout risk. We queried the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) registry (10/2015-12/2023) for patients reaching the 6-month exception form (k=3 form). CR was defined as cumulative tumor diameter (CTD)=0 and AFP≤20 ng/mL at k=3; durable CR additionally required CTD=0, AFP≤20, and no new LRT through 1 year after k=3. We compared waitlist outcomes between CR and non-CR (nCR) patients. A secondary analysis stratified a previously established low-risk cohort (baseline single lesion ≤3 cm, AFP≤20, Child-Pugh A, MELD-Na≤15) by LRT count required for CR. Of 20,240 HCC exception candidates, 6,764 were Child-Pugh A with MELD-Na ≤15 at k=3; 6,037 (89.2%) were within Milan at baseline, of whom 3,714 (61.5%) achieved CR. From k=3, CR candidates had lower cumulative dropout incidence than nCR at 1 and 2 years (5.9% vs. 11.6%; 9.0% vs. 15.8%; p<0.001), with no difference in transplant rate (65.7% vs. 66.0%; 74.7% vs. 75.0%; p=0.12). At 18 months post-listing, 331 of 584 (56.7%) within-Milan CR candidates achieved durable CR and subsequently had lower dropout than those losing CR (3.7% vs. 13.5% at 1 y; 7.2% vs. 20.8% at 2 y; p<0.001). In the secondary analysis, CR conferred a dropout advantage among low-risk patients requiring 1 LRT (3.9% vs. 4.7% at 1 y; 6.0% vs. 11.9% at 2 y; p=0.002) but not ≥2 LRT (7.6% vs. 7.8% at 1 y; 12.2% vs. 10.3% at 2 y; p=0.40). CR was associated with a lower dropout risk than nCR, particularly when CR was durable. This advantage was amplified among baseline low-risk patients, though only in those requiring a single LRT. These findings identify HCC candidates with substantially lower dropout risk but no corresponding reduction in transplant priority, suggesting that exception policy could be better calibrated to individual risk.
items.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
